title: Trades by Matt: How I became consistently profitable (Base Hits)
author: Trades by Matt
text:
[Góc nhìn từ Trades by Matt] Bạn tập trung vào những “base hits” 10‑15 điểm, tránh “home run” lớn, và luôn đặt rủi ro rõ ràng để giữ kỷ luật.
Điểm cốt lõi trong video:
- Sử dụng chiến lược “base hits” 10‑15 điểm trên Nasdaq (phút 02:52)
- Đặt rủi ro rõ ràng và chấp nhận rủi ro 100% khi vào lệnh (phút 04:57)
Kiểm chứng & Điểm mù thực chiến:
- Nhận định (chưa kiểm chứng): Nếu không đạt được mục tiêu, nên thoát ngay và chờ cơ hội mới (không đưa dữ liệu kiểm chứng)
- Điểm khuất cần lưu ý: Không đề cập đến spread, thanh khoản, hoặc kích thước mẫu backtest
- Phù hợp khi: Thị trường cổ phiếu, chỉ số Nasdaq, giao dịch ngắn hạn với khối lượng lớn | Dễ hỏng khi: Thị trường ngoại hối, thị trường tiền điện tử có thanh khoản thấp, hoặc khi có spread lớn
Bạn đã bao giờ thử áp dụng “base hits” 10‑15 điểm trong giao dịch thực tế chưa?
Nguồn (phụ đề tự động, tóm tắt bởi AI): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MlxpfJ0vphI

So, first things first, I wasn't always a person that did base hits. Um you can go [music] back plenty of time on my YouTube channel and see that. I don't ever want to feel that way again. I don't want to ever put myself in that position again. What does it look like moving forward? So, fast forward, you know, Q1 of 2025, I'm pulling out over $300,000 in 85 days trading on Apex, only doing base hits, looking for 10-point winners on the Nasdaq, and it solidified in my brain that this was the right approach, and [music] it has been what I've been doing consistently since then, and it has dramatically shifted and shaped the way that I look at the markets and the [music] way I trade the markets. The idea from base hits comes from the movie Moneyball, and the quote is, "You get on base, we win. You don't, you lose." Moneyball was famous for, you know, the way that the MLB worked at the time, Major League Baseball. They were looking at big hitters, they wanted big hitters, >> [music] >> and a guy came in using stats and realized that if we just get on base, we're going to score more points than looking for someone who can hit home runs. So, taking that same approach, applying it to trading, I'm looking for base hits. So, for me, a base hit is anywhere from like 10 points to 15 points, depending on Usually, it's just 10 points. I trade the Nasdaq only. Uh this will depend based on what you are trading. >> [music] >> Different assets have different types of normal moves. Volatility obviously comes into play there as well, but for me on the Nasdaq, I'm consistently looking for 10 points. And that is a base hit. I want something that is repeatable and consistent over time. I'm not looking for these home run trades. They're super fun, right? I don't really want to time either side of it super well. I want to piggyback off of what the big players are doing and get in and out, take my base hit, and move on with my day, right? I can get filled up over little moves like that that are, you know, following my setups, following [music] risk really well, what I like to call cheap trades, and executing off of it. One of the questions I'm asked all the time is how do you pass trailing drawdown evaluations, right? Apex uses a trailing drawdown. There's a few firms out there that do. Do you have any tips and tricks for passing trailing drawdown? My answer is yes, base hits. Base hits are what solves the trailing drawdown problem.
